styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Churches, Roman ruins and the Alexander Nevsky Cathedral.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Roman Serdica, Ottoman mosques and communist-era sights.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Vitosha mountain hikes and the city's green parks.

stays.why: Walk to the cathedral, Roman ruins and the main sights. Best base for a first visit.
The main pedestrian street: cafés, shops and easy walking to everything central.
Quiet, leafy and local, with good metro and tram links to the centre.
Cheapest beds and lively student bars, but a metro or bus ride from the sights.

food: Try Bulgarian classics: shopska salad, banitsa pastry and grilled meats at a mehana (tavern).
Breakfast on the go: a warm banitsa with ayran (yogurt drink) from a bakery counter, cheap and filling.
Look for lunch menus (obedno menu) at local restaurants; they cost far less than dinner.
Vegetarians are well served: shopska salad, roasted peppers and sirene (white cheese) dishes are everywhere.
Tipping is modest, around 10%. Check the bill; some places add a service charge.
more_time: Day trip to Rila Monastery: a UNESCO site in the mountains, roughly 2 hours each way. Check bus times on the day.
Add Plovdiv, a historic old town about 2 hours by bus or train, for a night or a long day.
Hike Vitosha mountain: take the cable car or a bus up and walk back down in a half day.

recommend.why: Two nights cover the cathedral, Roman ruins and old centre at an easy pace. Add a night for a Vitosha or Rila day trip.

month_notes: Coldest month: highs near 5°C, lows around -4°C. Pack a warm coat and boots.
Still cold, highs near 9°C. Fewer tourists and lower prices.
Mild but wet: about 12 rain days. Bring an umbrella.
Spring warms up to 17°C. Good for walking and Vitosha hikes.
Pleasant at 21°C but the wettest month, around 14 rain days.
Warm and green at 25°C. Long evenings and outdoor cafés.
Hot and dry: highs near 28°C, only about 6 rain days.
Similar to July: hot and mostly dry. Good for mountain escapes.
Warm and dry at 24°C. One of the best months to visit.
Cooler at 18°C with autumn colour. Still good for sightseeing.
Chilly at 12°C and wetter. Bring layers.
Cold again: highs near 7°C, lows around -1°C. Festive city lights.

climate_guide.summary: Continental climate with four clear seasons: cold winters, warm dry summers and a wet spring.

items.title: Best time: May to September
items.text: Warm days from 21°C to 28°C. Ideal for walking the city and hiking Vitosha.

items.title: Cold winters (December to February)
items.text: Highs of 5–9°C and lows below freezing. Snow is possible. Pack a warm coat, hat and boots.

items.title: Wettest in spring
items.text: May has about 14 rain days. Showers pass quickly; carry a small umbrella.

items.title: Driest in late summer
items.text: July, August and September have only 5–6 rain days. Reliable sunshine.

items.title: Mild, pleasant autumn
items.text: September and October stay at 18–24°C. Good light and fewer crowds.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Comfortable shoes for uneven pavements, layers for cool evenings, and a rain jacket in spring and autumn.

transit.best: Walk the centre; use the metro for the airport and longer hops.

modes.text: Line 4 links the airport to the centre in about 40 minutes. Cheap and fast.
Buses, trams and trolleybuses run 05:00–23:00, plus four night lines. A single ticket is about 1.60 лв; a day card about 4 лв.
Taxis are yellow. Use OK Supertrans or the Ridenow app to avoid overcharging.
Not needed in the city; parking is hard. Rent only for trips outside Sofia.
The centre is walkable, but pavements are uneven and potholed. Watch your step.
Bank cards and Apple/Google Pay work on metro gates and ticket readers.
